lines.locked: The ring's asleep, love. It wakes when the valley's had a proper fright and come through it. Come back when the east meadow's quiet again.
offer: Oh! You can see the ring? Most folk walk straight through it.
It goes to Gloamwood: lanterns, moss, the kindest dark you'll ever meet. But the ring's gone sleepy.
Bring me six flowers and three wild herbs, and I'll sing it awake. Deal?
lines.yes: Lovely. Any flowers will do. The ring isn't fussy, only hungry.
lines.wait: Six flowers and three wild herbs, love. The ring's yawning but it isn't up yet.
done: There we are. Hear that? Like a kettle just before it sings.
Step into the middle and think of lanterns. You'll land in Lanternfall.
lines.travel: The ring's humming. Off to Lanternfall?
lines.home: Back to the forest, or somewhere further?
lines.wrong_arc: The ring doesn't open for you.

mail.text: There's a fairy ring by the forest path that hums at dusk. I keep the moths that keep it. If you've got a minute and a few flowers, come and find me. - Liesl

lines.locked: The dune winds are wrong this season. We sail when the valley's had two good stories told about it. Not before.
offer: You've got the look of someone who walks too far for fun.
This wagon sails the sand to Mirage Post, the last well before the Sunscorch. Three days of dunes.
I'm short on bread and rope. Four loaves, three coils, and you ride free. Yes?
lines.yes: Good. The desert eats rope and the crew eats bread. Bring both.
lines.wait: Four bread, three rope. The wind's turning, friend.
done: That'll see us across. Climb aboard, mind the water barrels.
The sails go up at a word. Mirage Post, and then the whole Expanse.
lines.home: Back to the coast, or on somewhere else?

mail.text: A sand-sail caravan is beached past the dunes on your coast. We cross to the Sunscorch Expanse when we're stocked. Bring bread if you want a ride. - Sefa

lines.locked: Night train's not running. Line's tied up in somebody's paperwork. When your name means something in this valley, come back and we'll talk tickets.
offer: You're the one moving up in this town. I hear things in a ticket booth.
There's a night train to Ironline. Rail town, coal smoke, a Baron who thinks he owns every track. He's squeezing the whole line dry.
My engine's cold. Ten coal and three iron bars and she runs again. You in?
lines.yes: Coal for the firebox, iron for the couplings. I'll keep the booth lit.
lines.wait: Ten coal, three iron bars. She won't run on promises.
done: Hear that? That's a firebox catching. Best sound in the world.
Ticket's on the house. Junction City, end of the line. Watch your pockets.
lines.home: Back to town, or another stop?

mail.text: There's a ticket booth by the town square nobody uses. I run the night train out of it, when I've got coal. Stop by. Could be work in it. - Hollis

entry.label: the sled run up to Frostpeak

lines.locked: Up there? Not yet. The Reach is no place for someone who hasn't seen a few hard winters of trouble. Come back later on in your story.
offer: So you want to go higher than the mountain. Everybody does, once.
Past the clouds there's Frostpeak Reach: Hearthhold, the glaciers, and the Summit, where something big sleeps in the ice.
Four wool for your coat and six coal for the sled's warmer. Then I'll take you. Agreed?
lines.yes: Good. And eat something before you come back. Cold eats the hungry first.
lines.wait: Four wool, six coal. I'm not hauling a frozen hero down the hill.
done: There. Wrap up. Hold on to the rail, not to me.
Hearthhold's at the top. Ask for the hot spring. Everyone does.
lines.home: Down the mountain, or somewhere else?

mail.text: There's a sled run off the mountain that goes up past the clouds to Frostpeak Reach. I guide it. If you're tough enough by now, come and ask. - Brannoch

lines.locked: Too much weather up there for a passenger, I'm afraid. When the Star Crystal's nearly whole again the winds will calm. Then we fly.
offer: Ahoy! Well, ahoy-ish. There's no water. Ahoy anyway!
Above the sky islands, higher than the station even, are the Windward Isles. Breezehaven. Storm Shelf. And the Roc.
My envelope's torn and the lift crystal's gone dim. Four cloth and one Refined Crystal and we sail. Aye?
lines.yes: Splendid! I'll be right here, being a penguin in a basket.
lines.wait: Four cloth, one Refined Crystal. Penguins can't fly, you see. Balloons can.
done: Breezehaven, here we come. Don't look down. Actually, do. It's lovely.
lines.home: Down to the meadow, or onward?
lines.wrong_arc: The balloon's basket is full of penguin. There's no room.

mail.text: A balloon is tied up in the east meadow. It is captained by a penguin. That is me. I fly to the Windward Isles when I have a crew and a patch. - Capt. Zephyr

lines.locked: Madame Aurum doesn't send the car for just anyone. Make a bigger name for yourself, then I'll come back with the engine running.
offer: Nice place. Small. Honest. Gilt City is neither.
Madame Aurum runs the casinos, the gardens and the Vaults under them. She's heard of you. She wants to meet.
The invitation costs twelve stacks of cash and one gold bar. Call it a cover charge. In?
lines.yes: Wonderful. I'll keep the leather seats warm.
lines.wait: Twelve stacks and a gold bar. Madame is patient. I am less so.
done: Pleasure doing business. Mind the step, it's real gold.
Grand Plaza in an hour. Smile for the statues.
lines.home: Back to the farm, or another address?

mail.text: Madame Aurum of Gilt City sends her regards and a car. It is parked by your farm. Do not keep it waiting. - P.
